title: Finite coefficient realization commutes with ordinary direct image
statement: Let X and Y be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], f : X → Y any scheme morphism, and Λ a finite commutative ring with the discrete topology. Use the continuous-function coefficient ring sheaves, module categories and canonical realization functors of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and the ordinary module direct image with its specified precomposition-on-functions scalar map [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. There is a natural isomorphism realization_X ⋙ f_*^module ≅ f_*^fixed ⋙ realization_Y, where f_*^fixed is direct image of fixed-Λ module sheaves on the pro-etale sites.

source.place: lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules and definition-pushforward; explicit scalar-map calculation for the finite coefficient model

proof.text: The scalar map from constant scalars commutes with direct image: after precomposing with the sheafification unit this is the identity saying that precomposition of a constant function is constant. The sheafification adjunction gives the required equality of ring-presheaf maps. This is scalarDirectImage_square in the Lean proof.

Let E_T embed fixed-ring module sheaves into constant-ring module presheaves, and let U_T forget a finite-coefficient module sheaf and restrict its scalars along the constant-scalar map. The sheafification adjunction has invertible counit, hence U_T is fully faithful. Its unit is invertible on E_T(F), since the underlying abelian presheaf of F is already a sheaf. Thus E_T is naturally isomorphic to realization_T followed by U_T. These are Mathlib PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction, its isomorphism-of-counit instance, and isIso_toSheafify.

Restriction U_Y after the module direct image equals, up to the identity natural isomorphism on sections, U_X followed by presheaf precomposition with pro-etale base change. The identity is linear because of step 1. The maps and their inverse are identities, so their naturality is the sectionwise reflexive equality. This is restrictionDirectImageIso.

Whisker the preceding isomorphism by realization_X and use the unit identifications of step 2 on both sides. Both underlying fixed-ring direct images are precomposition with the same base-change functor. This yields an isomorphism of the desired functors after postcomposition by U_Y. Cancel the fully faithful U_Y by Mathlib Functor.fullyFaithfulCancelRight. No nontriviality, nonempty-scheme or properness hypothesis was used.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteCoefficientRealization_directImage
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    [TopologicalSpace Λ] [DiscreteTopology Λ] :
    Nonempty (finiteCoefficientRealization X Λ ⋙ finiteCoefficientModuleDirectImage f Λ ≅
      lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f ⋙ finiteCoefficientRealization Y Λ)
